subject: Deployment mode & compliance next steps (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: john.doe@elarahealth.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode & compliance next steps (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)

Hi John —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align with your security and deployment requirements: 

- Summary of requirements we heard: Elara needs PHI support (HIPAA) for clinical notes ingestion, SOC 2 Type II evidence for vendor assessments, a signed BAA, and the ability to support an audit trail for model inference.
- Deployment modes discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity (isolated GPU pool, predictable throughput), Private VPC / on‑prem (for full network isolation).
- Our recommendation: start with Dedicated reserved capacity to validate throughput & latency with your workload, then migrate to Private VPC when you're ready for full isolation/audit scope. If you require on‑prem, we can discuss packaging and timeline.

Action items we promised: 
1) Share our SOC 2 summary and the BAA draft — attached.
2) Send a short mutual action plan template for timelines & milestones.
3) Schedule a deeper security / architecture call with our infra team to cover encryption, KMS/HSM, logging, and audit artifacts.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-summary.pdf; BAA_draft_redwood_2027.docx; I'll follow up with the MAP in the next email.

Would you be available for a 30‑min security deep dive on Wednesday (5/12) or Thursday (5/13)?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
(555) 555-0156
From: John Doe <john.doe@elarahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@elarahealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance next steps (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)

Thanks Neha — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Given that we'll be processing PHI and need to scope for regulatory audits, Elara prefers Private VPC or on‑prem for production. However, we'd be open to a staged approach if Dedicated can guarantee the required isolation and audit artifacts in the interim.
- Can you confirm the types of evidence you can provide for SOC 2 (full report, SOC 2 bridge letter, or summary)? We need enough to satisfy our procurement security team.
- Encryption at rest and in transit: please confirm KMS options and whether customer‑managed keys are supported in Dedicated/Private.
- Throughput: we typically need 50–100 concurrent sessions with median prompt sizes ~1k tokens and occasional bursts. Can you share expected latency numbers for Dedicated vs Hosted for that profile?

We'd like to move quickly — please send whatever SOC2 evidence you can and your suggested next steps for getting a Dedicated environment provisioned for load testing.

—John
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@elarahealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance next steps (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)

Hi John — thanks for the clear list. Answering each point below and attaching the items we discussed.

- SOC 2 evidence: attached is our SOC 2 Type II summary (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-summary.pdf). We can provide a redacted full report under an NDA if needed; alternatively customers often accept the Type II summary + our SOC 3 for preliminary reviews.
- BAA: attached draft (BAA_draft_redwood_2027.docx). We're happy to iterate.
- KMS / encryption: we support customer‑managed keys via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private VPC deployments. For on‑prem we support HSM integrations; we can share architecture diagrams on the security call.
- Throughput / latency: for 1k token median prompts and 50–100 concurrent sessions, Dedicated typically hits p50 latency ~150–300ms per token (depends on model/quantization) and scales predictably with reserved GPUs. Hosted will have slightly higher variance; we'll provide benchmark numbers in the load test.

I've attached a short mutual action plan (elara_mutual_action_plan.xlsx) with proposed milestones: provision Dedicated test cluster -> run load tests -> sign BAA -> plan Private VPC rollout.

Next steps:
- I'll schedule the security deep‑dive for Thursday 5/13 at 11am PT unless you prefer a different time.
- If you can confirm that timeline, we'll provision a Dedicated test environment (1 week lead) and share test credentials and benchmarking instructions.

Attachment: elara_mutual_action_plan.xlsx; Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-summary.pdf; BAA_draft_redwood_2027.docx

On Thu, 13 May we can bring in our infra/security SMEs (Dylan + Marissa) to cover KMS, audit logging, and evidence packaging.

Best,
Neha
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@elarahealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance next steps (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)

John — quick note from infra:

Short answer: Dedicated reserved capacity is the fastest path to validate throughput and auditability. It gives you an isolated GPU pool, customer KMS support, and access to our extended logging hooks (token tracing, request/response audit log exports).

If you expect to require full network isolation and customer‑owned control plane for audits, Private VPC is the end state. Typical cadence we see: Dedicated test for 2–6 weeks -> evidence capture and audit prep -> Private VPC cutover (4–8 weeks depending on region and infra approvals).

I'll bring sample audit log exports and a checklist to the 5/13 call. I also dropped the HubSpot deal link for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ELR-5791

Thanks — Dylan
From: John Doe <john.doe@elarahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@elarahealth.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance next steps (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)

Thanks everyone — this sounds good. We'll proceed with the staged approach: Dedicated reserved capacity for validation and throughput testing, with the plan to migrate to Private VPC for production once audit scope is confirmed.

Please go ahead and: 
- Provision the Dedicated test environment and send credentials + benchmarking instructions.
- Send DocuSign link for the BAA (we can sign once legal reviews).
- Share the additional SOC 2 artifacts under NDA if you can (redacted full report or bridge letter).

I'll have security@elarahealth.com join the 5/13 call.

John
